 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accumulated a game-high 30 points (11-of-20 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists and one block over 29 minutes to propel the Thunder to a 114-75 blowout win over the Wizards. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 points in just three quarters to help Oklahoma City cruise to a relatively easy 39-point victory on the second night of a back-to-back. The 28-year-old scoring machine is averaging a sublime 29.9 points through 10 games, topping 30 points in exactly half of those contests. The Thunder are back in action with a busy four-game week that includes back-to-back showdowns against the Trail Blazers in addition to road tilts against the Clippers and Kings.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander amassed 28 points (11-of-22 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in a blowout win over the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander continues to shoulder the bulk of the scoring workload for the injury-plagued Thunder who are without starters Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren. He came up short in his bid for a third consecutive 40-point performance, but that was mostly due to the fact that he wasn’t needed in the late stages of a one-sided affair. He got some significant help from youngsters Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain as the trio accounted for 75 of Oklahoma City’s 98 points through three quarters in a lopsided affair. The Thunder are back in action with a home matchup against the Wizards on Saturday.

 The Oklahoma City Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 The Thunder are going smaller in this game than they did against the Cavs with Aday Mara heads to the bench and Jared McCain returns to the starting lineup. Mara will go back to being a backup center while McCain might get more minutes in this game. If McCain is available, he might be worth grabbing if you need some points and 3’s.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 42 points (11-of-26 FGs, 15-of-19 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one block and five three-pointers in the 124-116 victory over the Cavaliers on Wednesday. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander has destroyed the Cavaliers in the last two games. The two-time defending MVP has 85 points and two wins against Cleveland going all the way back to Monday. Gilgeous-Alexander can reach heights few players in the NBA can. He showed that again Wednesday and will likely continue to have some monster nights while the Thunder are missing multiple starters.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 43 points (14-of-35 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal, two blocks and four three-pointers in the Thunder’s 117-112 victory over the Cavaliers on Monday. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander had only eclipsed 30 points twice in the first six games of the season before dropping 43 points in the win over the Cavaliers Monday. The 28-year-old point guard had a full stat line that also included four rebounds, eight assists, one steal, two blocks and four three-pointers. Given the amount of injuries the Thunder are dealing with, Gilgeous-Alexander is going to continue to have nights like this to keep the team afloat, which is a boon for his fantasy value.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 26 points (10-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Since the October 25 game against the Clippers in which Oklahoma City lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, Gilgeous-Alexander has shot 49.1 percent from the field and 5-of-17 from beyond the arc. Of course, the Thunder have also lost Chet Holmgren since last Sunday, which allows opposing teams to devote even more attention to slowing down SGA. Fantasy managers will hope his efficiency doesn’t take too big a hit in the weeks to come. Oklahoma City plays four games next week, starting with two against the Cavaliers on Monday (away) and Wednesday (home).

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Monday’s win over the Suns with 26 points (11-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one three-pointer. 
 In the aftermath of the injuries to Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams, some may have expected Gilgeous-Alexander to shoot until his arm fell off. That didn’t happen, as the reigning MVP got his points while also trusting his teammates. SGA recorded just three assists, but he shot the ball well and notched his second consecutive games of 25 points or more. Oklahoma City plays two more games in Week 2, starting with the Mavericks on Wednesday.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander amassed 34 points (13-of-26 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 On a night when he saw three teammates leave the game with injuries, Gilgeous-Alexander carried the Thunder in the third quarter. The reigning MVP scored 16 of his 34 points in the period, shooting 7-of-11 from the field. SGA went cold in the fourth, but his teammates provided enough help to keep Oklahoma City undefeated. The Thunder play three games in Week 2, starting with the Suns on Monday.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Thursday’s win over the Nuggets with 17 points (6-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander started extremely slowly on Thursday, scoring just two points on 0-of-6 shooting in the first half. The reigning MVP scored 15 points in the second half, but it wasn’t enough to extend his streak of at least 20-point games to 142. Gilgeous-Alexander doesn’t have many nights like this, so fantasy managers have no reason to worry. The Thunder host the Clippers on Sunday in their final Week 1 game.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder with 32 points (13-of-27 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, three blocks and three three-pointers in a 116-104 win over the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 The back-to-back MVP started his campaign for three straight with a statement performance against the team that eliminated them from the playoffs last season. He somehow improved his game even more this summer, and it was on full display in the win. He was one of the top few picks in fantasy basketball drafts and was more than worth the early selection. He’ll look to stay hot in their home opener against the Nuggets on Friday.

 Ajay Mitchell recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long.

 Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.

 Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. The final three points came on a 35-footer as time expired, giving Portland a 17-point lead heading into the fourth quarter. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.
